page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Cost Optimized family. Built on QEMU virtualization, it is provisioned with 2 shared vCPUs derived from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. Memory is configured at 4.0 GB of system RAM, allocating approximately 1.95 GB per core. The server includes 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating without discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations position the cx23 in the lower tiers of raw processing capability, reflecting its shared-core architecture. In computational testing, the server attained a stress-ng single-core score of 1028.88 and a multi-core score of 2016.78, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 2394.06. Geekbench testing returned scores of 713.0 for single-core execution and 1233.0 across multiple cores. Memory subsystem testing demonstrated an uncached read bandwidth of 20.91 GB/sec and a write throughput of 16.93 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 2.52 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 1.77 GB/sec.

Given the shared vCPU design and entry-level throughput, this server delivers practical cost efficiency for lightweight environments where high uninterrupted compute density is unnecessary. The 40 GB NVMe storage provides rapid local I/O compared to network-attached disks, compensating for limited multi-threaded computational headroom. Hetzner Cloud cx23 is best aligned with lightweight utility workloads, including basic web serving, edge routing, low-traffic staging environments, small background automation tasks, and simple microservices.
